headline.en: Land right on a note, don't slide into it. That's what makes a harmony ring.

detail.en: Hear it in your head first

text.en: Two to warm up. Sing each note back after the guide, and watch where it lands.
Round 1: five notes. Listen, think it, then land on it.
Round 2: five more. Closer to the middle this time?

measures.en: Your stars are for where your second round's notes landed: close to the middle, and without sliding in.

headline.en: A scoop is sliding up into a note from below. It's a habit, and habits change.

detail.en: Starts low, slides up to the note
Think the note before you breathe in

text.en: Slide up into the first two on purpose, then start the next two right on the note. Watch the trails.
Four notes, each one clean. Listen, think it, then land on it.

measures.en: Your stars are for where your notes landed: close to the middle, and without sliding in. A note that slid in counts half.

headline.en: Do is your note. Re, mi, fa and so are the steps up from it: 2, 3, 4 and 5.

detail.en: A jump of three and of five up

text.en: Hear the pair, then two quiet beats: hear it in your head. Then sing it. Did you hear it before you sang?
Do to so, so to do, do to mi, la (below) to do. Each note short and separate.

measures.en: Your stars are for landing each note of the leaps, close to the middle, without sliding in.

headline.en: The Westminster chimes: four little tunes on four notes, each note its own clean start.

detail.en: Each note separate, like a bell
Think it, breathe, start on it

text.en: Your Bullseye round first: five notes, to see how far you've come.
All four chimes, on "dong". After each one, it's your turn.

measures.en: Your stars are for landing all sixteen notes, close to the middle. A note that slid in counts half, so one scoop costs a little, never a star.

headline.en: Two notes a little apart beat: a slow wah-wah. The beats slow down as you get closer, and stop when you're there.

text.en: Listen to each with the drone, as often as you like, then choose.

why.en: A beats against the drone. B is smooth: it's in tune.
B is a little flat, so it beats. A is smooth.
A beats fastest, B slower, C not at all: C is in tune.

prompt.en: Is the guide sharp or flat?

why.en: It's a little above the drone: sharp.

prompt.en: Is the guide sharp or flat?

why.en: It's a little under the drone: flat.

prompt.en: Is the guide sharp or flat?

why.en: Just under: flat. Closer than the last one, so the beating is slower.

text.en: Start a little under the drone, then slide up slowly until the beating stops. Headphones help: one ear off.
Hold your note over the drone until it rings. Neck, jaw and tongue soft.

measures.en: Your stars are for how closely you held your note to the drone: within 10 cents is locked. Was your neck soft?

headline.en: A drone's strongest partners are the fifth and the octave. Both ring true, so they're easy to lock.

detail.en: It gets smoother when you find it

text.en: So, then do, over the low drone. Find where each one goes smooth.
Hold so, then do, over the drone an octave below. Neck, jaw and tongue soft.

measures.en: Your stars are for how closely you locked so and do to the drone. Did each get smoother when you found it?

headline.en: Stepping away and back is where pitch slips. Come home to exactly where you were.

text.en: Do, re, do. Make the last do the same as the first.
Echo each one, over the drone: do-re-do, do-ti-do, do-so-do.

measures.en: Your stars are for every note's centre, and most of all for coming home to the same do.

headline.en: The end of a breath and repeated notes pull you flat. Slow the breath out, and think up. Never squeeze.

detail.en: Then let the air out slowly
As the note goes on, and on the way down

text.en: Mi, mi, mi, re, do: keep the repeated mi from sinking.
Two long notes over the drone: do, then so. Keep each one up to its very end.

measures.en: Your stars are for where each long note sat and whether it sagged or crept by its end: under 10 cents is steady.

headline.en: A cowboy song over a drone on your note. Lock the long notes, keep the rest in tune.

detail.en: The long do rings with the drone
The last long note, on re

text.en: Your Bullseye round first: five notes, to see how far you've come.
Sing it with the guide, at your own pace.
Now on your own, over the drone. Neck, jaw and tongue soft.

measures.en: Your stars are for the long do locked to the drone and every other note's centre.
